title: Adaptive token-priority shaping - personal scratchpad
content:
2026-03-12 / quick log (Ivy)

Context: playing with an idea to reduce long-tail latency for low-priority requests without hurting head-of-line latency for critical requests. Goal: per-request token-priority shaping in the request router + light-weight feedback loop from the runtime.

High-level idea (brain dump):
- Each incoming request carries a priority score (from client or inferred): p in [0,1] where 1 = highest.
- Router maps p -> shaping profile: window-size, prefetch-ahead, kv-cache affinity, batch-slot weight.
- Low p -> encourage batching / pack into slower batch pools with higher batching thresholds and optional micro-caching; high p -> route to low-latency pool with smaller batches and prewarmed KV caches.
- Add feedback: runtime reports per-token tail latency and token generation rate per pool; router adjusts mapping every minute with simple PID-ish controller to respect p95 SLO on high tier while maximizing throughput on low tier.

Observations from prototype (yesterday):
- Synthetic mix (70% low p, 30% high p) on dev rig: throughput up 18% when low-p traffic routed to a single dense batch pool, but p95 for high-p rose by ~12ms when we increased low-p batch size aggressively.
- Micro-caching of common prefixes (low-p pool) reduces token work but introduced occasional cache-thrashing (eviction bursts) when sequence variety spiked.
- Telemetry gap: we can't easily attribute KV-cache hits to a request without adding a request id tag on KV keys. Doing so increases KV meta overhead by ~5% (measured).

Concrete TODOs (prioritized):
1) Short experiment: add request-id tag to KV keys for just the low-p pool and enable sampling (1%) to measure attribution without full overhead. Estimate: 2 days (code + infra metric). Assignee: me.
2) Safety net: implement a hard p95 guard in router so that any config change that would push high-tier p95 beyond target triggers an automatic rollback. Use existing rollout infra (see rollout playbook). Assignee: Noah.
3) Controller tuning: quick heuristics first (linear mapping p->batch_size, clip by pool capacity), follow-up with simple exponential smoothing. Make it toggleable via feature flag. Assignee: Lina.
4) Small perf microbench: run token-generation microbench (fixed model, long sequence 4k tokens) to measure memory pressure pattern between shaped vs unshaped routing. Add heap samples every 30s. Assignee: me + SRE.
5) Postmortem checklist item: if low-p cache thrash => capture KV eviction window and top-10 evicted keys. Add to log aggregation. Assignee: SRE (ticket).

Experiment plan details:
- Envs: staging-dense1 (GPUs: a100-40c) for low-p pool; staging-lowlat (T4-like) for high tier.
- Metric targets: high-p p50 < 18ms, high-p p95 < 60ms; low-p p95 unconstrained but track cost-per-token.
- Sampling flags: request.priorityTag (client-provided), otherwise infer via route (heuristic: embedding length / route type).

Quick pseudocode for router mapping (very rough):

// map priority p in [0,1] to batch target
function batch_target(p) {
  // base: prefer smaller batches for high priority
  base = round( (1 - p) * 64 )  // 0 -> 64, 1 -> 0
  // clip to pool capacity
  return clamp(base, 4, 64)
}

Controller sketch:
- Observe: high_p95_current, high_p95_target
- If high_p95_current > target + slack -> reduce low-p batch_target by 20% (min clamp)
- Else if high_p95_current < target - slack -> gradually increase low-p batch_target to improve throughput

Unresolved questions / risks:
- Fairness: client may falsely tag requests as high priority to get better latency. Need auth/quotas per customer to prevent abuse. Work with product.
- Billing: shaped routing could change token accounting (e.g., prefetching). Need to ensure billing reflects actual tokens consumed. Loop in finance.
- Observability: attribution requires adding more request metadata to logs. Storage cost tradeoff.

Notes-to-self (quick):
- Talk to Lina about adding a lightweight per-pool ttl-based caching policy (prefix-safe eviction). Might reduce thrash.
- Open PR to add request-id sample to KV keys: draft already exists at PR 879 (linked above). Rebase before running experiment.
- Check JIRA-RINF-2481 for previous notes on fairness gating; looks like a related spike from Jan.

Today (2026-03-13) immediate steps:
- Morning (1h): rebase PR 879, add 1% sampling flag, run unit tests.
- Midday (2h): implement request-id tagging toggle in router config + add metrics for kv-hit-by-sampled-req.
- Afternoon (3h): coordinate with SRE to spin up staging-dense1 and run the microbench (heap sampling).
- End of day: quick writeup (2 paragraphs) summarizing results, file into confluence:adaptive-serving-notes and link to JIRA ticket.

Quick logs (errors / weirds):
- Saw unexpected 500s in low-p pool when prefetch queue length > 140; likely a queue sizing bug in the packer. Need to add guard rails to packer to never enqueue > capacity.
- Warmup: low-latency pool warmup times vary by model size; for 70B warmed from snapshot took ~16s vs 8s for 13B. Consider prewarm for scheduled traffic.

Small checklist before experiment:
- [ ] Ensure PR 879 rebased and CI green
- [ ] Feature flag toggles present and default off
- [ ] SRE channel + infra ticket created for staging nodes
- [ ] Metrics dashboard templated (p50/p95/p99 per pool + kv-hit-rate + cost/token)

Random thought: could we add a token-credit system per-customer where credits buy low-latency routing? Combines billing + fairness. Prototype later if pilot looks good.

End of notes. Keep this messy. Update as I make progress.
